overview: Chlamydia is a common sexually transmitted infection that can occur in both men and women. It is caused by a bacterium called Chlamydia trachomatis. It is easily treated and cured with antibiotics.
symptoms: bleeding between menstrual periods or after sex
pain or discomfort in the lower abdomen
chronic oozing lesions around anorectal region
diagnosis: swab-collected samples from genital (vaginal or urethral), anal and oropharyngeal sites
treatment: antibiotic tablets including doxycycline or azithromycin
prevention: correct and consistent use of condoms during sex
complications: chronic oozing lesions around anorectal region
key_facts: In 2020, an estimated 128.5 million new infections with Chlamydia trachomatis occurred worldwide among adults aged 15 to 49 years.
The global prevalence among people aged 15–49 years was estimated to be 4.0% for women and 2.5% for men in 2020.
